🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran’s dams were just linked to its hidden missile bases in a new report... and blowing one up works like a weapon of mass destruction

Nobody has proposed bombing them, and the report itself admits the link is unproven, but the idea is now out there.

Michael Yon, a former Green Beret and war correspondent, has spent years on what he calls hydraulic warfare.

Whoever controls a big dam can flood the people downstream or cut their water, and breaking one can take down every dam below it.

China learned that in 1975, when one failure knocked out about 60 more and killed as many as a quarter million people.

Michael on what a reservoir really is:

“So when you build a dam, you’re generally speaking you’re building a WMD over your own head, right?”

Iran’s Karun River runs through a chain of dams, farmland and cities on its way to the Gulf.

Could anyone strike a base next to one and promise the water stays put?

@Michael_Yon  @WeTheBrandon

🇺🇸🇮🇷 How many troops would regime change in Iran take? Try 2.5 million more than America has to send

Bombing a government and removing one are two very different jobs.

Larry Johnson, a former CIA analyst, runs the numbers on the second one.

He puts the Revolutionary Guard at about 1 million men, and since an attacker normally needs 3 soldiers for every defender, Washington would have to find roughly 2.5 million more troops, while its Patriot stockpile can't be rebuilt before 2030.

Larry on the planning behind another round of strikes:

"We're into the land of magical thinking. Only it's black magic."

He says a friend with ties to Central Command expects strikes right after Trump's Shenzhen summit this week.

If that's true, what's the plan for day 4, when the missiles run low and the regime is still standing?

@WeTheBrandon @NewSonof
